The growing presence of artificial intelligence systems has led to a significant rise in the need for their explanations. Transparency and stakeholder trust are achieved by reducing the opacity of these systems through the provision of explanations. In this paper, we explore the interconnection between explainability and transparency in the context of machine learning, with a focus on their respective methodologies and tools. A unified framework for understandability is presented, along with a detailed analysis of the relationship between explainability and transparency. Ultimately, we identify key areas for further investigation and development in this field. Additionally, we have created the RE reasoner toolkit, a set of tools and techniques that can aid researchers and developers in crafting and evaluating tailored methods for explaining machine learning decisions. This tool is now accessible online and is being continuously updated. All of the tool's source code can be obtained freely through the RE GitHub repository. It is comprised of nine software components: five dedicated to the creation of custom explanations, three focused on the extraction of existing explanations, and a final one used for the joint exploration of reasons and their applicability to specific predictive tasks. Moreover, the tool includes 20 exemplary reasons across four subjects, which can be utilized for inspiration or as baseline solutions. As a fully interactive application, the tool enables users to generate, inspect, compare, and reason about custom explanations, as well as access existing ones. It is intended to support researchers in developing innovative solutions and testing these explanations against real-world scenarios, with a focus on improving the understandability of machine learning systems. In the long term, we aspire for this tool to serve as a hub where researchers can share their methods for generating tailored explanations, and engage in theoretical and practical explorations of this field. By promoting interplay between research and practical applications, we believe that the tool can accelerate progress in this area and foster a more collaborative ecosystem among researchers and practitioners. In the realm of machine learning, explanations are increasingly crucial for gaining insight into predictive models, understanding their limitations, and rectifying any biases that may reside within them. In this study, we present the RE tool, which offers an intuitive and user-friendly platform for exploring the diverse realm of explanations. By providing access to state-of-the-art methods and a collection of 20 exemplary reasons across four subject areas, the RE tool serves as a cornerstone for this research, supporting both the creation of novel explanations and the in-depth analysis of existing ones. Furthermore, the RE tool facilitates interplay between research and practical applications, thereby enabling researchers to test their theories against real-world scenarios and evaluate the efficacy

Characterizing colorectal polyps histopathologically is crucial to personalize patient treatment and follow-up, ultimately reducing the risk of undetected invasive carcinomas. The process of polyp characterization involves examining tissue samples for malignancy and dysplasia using histological analysis. Recent advancements in deep learning have significantly improved medical pattern recognition accuracy; however, training these models necessitates vast collections of annotated medical images. In this context, we've developed UniToPatho, an extensive dataset consisting of 9536 annotated H&E stained patches derived from 292 whole-slide images, designed for deep learning-based classification and grading of colorectal polyps and adenomas. This dataset serves as a resource for researchers tackling the complex task of automating colorectal polyp characterization. Additionally, we've outlined a framework for establishing a collaborative, integrated pipeline involving pathologists for producing the necessary annotations, much like the ones employed in creating the UniToPatho dataset. Moreover, we've provided a set of carefully curated test images along with their annotations for assessment purposes, available on our website at https://retis.unicatt.it/untopatho/. We encourage researchers to partake in developing a state-of-the-art solution for classification and grading of colorectal polyps and adenomas by submitting their proposals to our challenge, accessible at https://retis.unicatt.it/untopatho/challenge/, where evaluation criteria and guidelines are outlined. To facilitate smooth development and testing of our challenge, we've integrated an unsupervised validation environment, allowing participants to evaluate their models during training, as well as in real-time conditions with our provided test dataset. The predictions submitted by participants are gathered in a public repository for reference and evaluation purposes. We anticipate that the technical advancements achieved through this challenge will contribute to the creation of efficient classification and grading models for colorectal polyps and adenomas. Ultimately, this will pave the way for the development of reliable computer-assisted diagnostic and prognostic tools, potentially transforming the treatment of colorectal cancer patients. To our knowledge, this is the first time that a deep learning-based challenge focused on characterization of gastrointestinal lesions has been launched, and we're excited to see the innovative approaches that researchers will bring to the table in solving this intricate problem. As a testament to the significance of this initiative, our team has received support from the International Symposium on Computer-Based Medical Systems (CBMS 2021), where the details of this challenge were presented, including a workshop and a competition for classification and grading of colorectal polyps and adenomas.

In the context of zero-error source coding, our investigation focuses on how much information a guessing adversary can gain. The underlying source coding problem is represented by a confusion graph, illustrating how source symbols can be distinguished from one another. The adversary's ability to successfully guess the source sequence is measured relative to its prior knowledge, with this measurement maximized over various source distributions. When the adversary follows a specific model where they only make a single guess and can perfectly match their guess to the true sequence, this measurement is known as the maximal leakage in literature and can be expressed as the maximum min-entropy leakage. We establish a comprehensive single-letter representation of the optimal normalized leakage in this adversarial scenario, along with a stochastic coding method that reaches this optimum. Interestingly, our analysis shows that both the optimal leakage and optimal compression rates are attainable by certain deterministic coding strategies, where these goals can be concurrently achieved. We expand upon the initial investigation to consider adversaries that submit multiple guesses and can tolerate a degree of sequence error. In this case, we identify tight lower and upper bounds for the more general leakage metric through the application of single-letter analysis. The upper bound for this leakage is shown to correspond to the maximum achievable rate in a standard source coding problem, and we can thus determine the optimal leakage by solving a specific convex optimization problem. Furthermore, our analysis reveals that adversaries following this corrected model can be equivalently portrayed as making a single guess at the most probable sequence within a certain tolerance distance, and we propose a novel guessing adversary that further generalizes this behavior. In this instance, we are able to determine tight lower and upper bounds for the leakage metric through the application of rate-distortion theory, where the adversary's ability to tolerate sequence error introduces a key distinction from prior literature. Lastly, our findings are expanded upon to include situations in which the source sequence comprises multiple symbols and is subject to specific constraints in a source coding problem with side information held by a guessing adversary. In this case, we can determine single-letter representations of both the optimal leakage and optimal compression rates by analyzing the adversary's expected gain in guessing the source sequence, where the adversary is assumed to employ an optimal guessing strategy that corresponds to repeated applications of a binary guess that maximizes the adversary's ability to successfully guess the source sequence. Here again, our analysis shows that both the optimal leakage and optimal compression rates are attainable by certain deterministic coding methods, where these goals can be concurrently achieved. In addition, our analysis in this situation reveals that the leakage metric reduces to a previously known literal value

Deep learning-trained generative models can function as a prior in under-determined inverse problems such as generating images from limited measurements, like a sparse dataset. A new hierarchical generative model called DepGen is introduced in this research, specifically designed for magnetic resonance imaging using a sparse measurement regime. DepGen consists of two separate generative networks, one creating variance reduction policies for image data and another producing noise patterns that mimic convolution effects, thereby enhancing the generative process. By introducing a directed acyclic graph to connect the two networks, DepGen efficiently samples images by sequentially addressing different aspect layers in an image. As a result of this structured sampling process, DepGen is able to outperform previous generative models and achieve state-of-the-art performance in reconstructing images from sparse measurements, specifically 10% of fully sampled data with an signal-to-noise ratio of 45.17 dB and mean square error of 2.17, using a standard MRI phantom image, and demonstrates its ability to recover burned patient images from sparse measurements with 2% of fully sampled data with an signal-to-noise ratio of 33.18 dB and mean square error of 5.03. A test reconstructing real MRI data from 10% of measurements further verifies the efficacy of DepGen. As an added benefit, the research finds that the noise pattern network can be used as a solver for under-determined inverse problems, outperforming conventional deep learning-based solvers in a numerical study. Code for this research is available on GitHub at the address https://github.com/visual-research/depgen. A video demonstrating the reconstructive capability of DepGen can be found at the address https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ypgHqCgz77g. To optimize a quantum circuit's parameters, we utilize a Bayesian approach as an auxiliary routine, evaluating its efficiency in contrast with alternative global optimizers.  The proposed technique leads to considerable reductions in circuit access frequency, typically the costliest QAOA component.  The framework performs well even at slow circuit repetition rates and with minimal quantum circuit measurements, yielding a reliable energy estimate.  Moreover, we investigate how our approach handles noise during circuit operation, discovering that for short circuits it remains resistant to disturbances.  The outcome of these findings supports the use of the suggested method as an adaptable tool to exploit the mixed capabilities of QAOA within imperfect quantum devices.  The potential of this technique to serve as a troubleshooting and performance assessment tool for quantum circuits is also explored. A versatile method has been devised for determining the overlap area between two ellipses. The proposed approach relies on computing segment areas between the two ellipses, using a secant line that intersects each ellipse at given points. The Gauss-Green formula enables calculation of an ellipse sector area, with a triangle either added to or subtracted from this sector area to obtain the segment area. For calculating the overlap area of two ellipses, the areas of relevant sectors and polygons are combined. The algorithm identifies the intersection points of two general ellipses by utilizing Ferrari's quartic formula to solve a resulting polynomial formed by combining the two ellipse equations, allowing for handling all cases of intersection points, along with handling singular cases where one ellipse passes through the other or they coincide. The proposed method has been implemented in C and validated through numerous tests with various input ellipses, demonstrating its efficiency and effectiveness. The processing speed was measured across a range of tests and it is revealed that this method remains computationally efficient regardless of the input ellipses' positions and orientations in space. The calculated overlap area is represented as a structured object which includes the area itself, the color coding (according to a predefined palette), the overlap ratio and the overlap duration. These metrics facilitate understanding of the overlap area and its dynamic behavior for any pair of input ellipses. The proposed scheme has numerous potential applications in mechanics and other fields to analyze complex geometric problems. The developed code also proposes options to save the calculated overlap area to image files for subsequent use in program development. The generated code can be utilized as a point of departure to analyze trajectories of moving objects represented as ellipses. The overlap area can be used to implement features like click-through reporting for areas of interest within the overlap region, thus enabling new features and applications. Ultimately, the code can serve as a foundation for designing more intricate shapes using a combination of polygons and ellipses. The proposed algorithm and its implementation can be utilized in a broad range of fields where geometric analysis plays a crucial role. Building upon the work by Wang et al. (2020) for reinforcement learning, we examine the continuous-time counterpart of Q-learning under the entropy-regularized exploratory process framework. To tackle the issue of non-markovian noise, we introduce a novel key concept, the instantaneous advantage rate function, $A$, which relates to the q-function, $\q$, by a first-order differential equation. Leveraging this connection, we formulate a continuous-time Q-learning framework. Consequently, we develop a simple expression for $\q$, depending on the exploration entropy function, $h$. Moreover, we show that solving this equation corresponds to finding the generator of a Markov process. To illustrate the applicability of our theory, we consider two examples: (i) a simple example in low dimensions; (ii) a scenario representing secure node connectivity in a random wireless sensor network. Our work extends the initial application outlined in Wang et al. (2020), but also allows for more extensive exploration of its implications. Furthermore, our results build upon those from Chen and Wang (2020) by including the handling of non-markovian noise. Lastly, our study bears similarities to that of Guan et al. (2021) in its application to wireless node connectivity, but surpasses their work in its level of detail and breadth of understanding. To facilitate replication, the code used for generating our figures and tables can be accessed at https://github.com/jcwb/Continuous-Time-Q-learning.git. Accurate vertebrae localization and identification are crucial in various medical applications related to spine disorder diagnosis and surgical planning. However, certain pathological variations (e.g., vertebral compression fractures, scoliosis, and vertebral fixation) and imaging conditions (e.g., limited visibility and metallic streak artifacts in CT scans) make this task challenging. To address these difficulties, this paper introduces an end-to-end deep learning network called VLN-Id, which combines local and global information to precisely identify and localize vertebrae. By leveraging a mixed convolutional neural network feature extraction approach that incorporates prior knowledge of anatomical structure interrelations, VLN-Id's identifier sub-network detects vertebral features with exceptional robustness against variations in appearance. Moreover, its locator sub-network, which utilizes relative position information from adjacent vertebrae, exhibits superior performance in the presence of metal artifacts. According to the results obtained from publicly available and institutionally provided spinal CT datasets containing diverse pathological cases, VLN-Id significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches. To facilitate reproducibility and evaluate its generalizability, the proposed method's source code, dataset extensions, and associated data have been made publicly available for download at github.com/CU-IDI/VLN-Id. Additionally, benchmarking results for recently introduced spinal CT segmentation tasks have been included in the supplementary material provided at idicwu.github.io/DeepVLN-Id/. VLN-Id has demonstrated remarkable performance in vertebral identification and localization, achieving average identification accuracies of 0.959 and 0.941 for cumulative and individual vertebral body classification, respectively. Furthermore, its average localization errors were 24.778 and 26.442 for cumulative and individual vertebral centerline mapping, indicating exceptional robustness against metal artifacts and other factors. Overall, the proposed VLN-Id method presents a cutting-edge approach to accurate vertebrae localization and identification in a range of spinal CT scans characterized by significant pathological variations. With its potential for widespread clinical application, VLN-Id is poised to significantly enhance the automated detection and localization of vertebral features in a variety of skeletal pathological conditions, ultimately contributing to improved diagnostic and surgical planning services. Moreover, its promising generalizability across various medical image types suggests its great potential for extension to other anatomical structures and imaging modalities. To this end, future network modifications to facilitate multiple anatomical structure localizations are being actively explored within our research group. The statistical behavior of these flow rates can be represented by normalized cumulants. This study applies the mathematical and topological structure of Markovian models to demonstrate the gauge invariance of the normalized cumulant-generating function. By taking advantage of this invariance, we have developed a streamlined method for the practical calculation of normalized cumulants. This method also generalizes the existing approaches to the microcanonical ensemble and the Gibbs grand ensemble. The disintegrating exoplanet K2-22b displays erratic patterns in transit best attributed to a dissipating debris cloud, as observed through WFIRST and Hubble space telescope data at wavelengths of 3.0 and 3.6 microns. Analysis of these observations reveals a planet that exists in a perpetual state of disintegration and reformulation. In this study, we undertake a comprehensive investigation of particle processes within the debris cloud that is responsible for the planet's disintegration. Utilizing ground-based spectrographs operating within the optical range, we are able to pinpoint fine-grained particles present in the cloud that is surrounding the planet. Our study indicates that these particles are composed primarily of silicates due to a lack of significant calcium signals. As a result, it is possible that these particles could be condensed from a surrounding atmosphere or steam released from the planet's interior as a result of intense tidal heating. In order to understand which environment is most prevalent, we conduct two detailed models of the debris cloud. In model 1, we find that the cloud's lifetime is estimated at approximately 49-92 days with a particle size of roughly 0.5 to 1.0 microns. In model 2, we discover that a more intricate network of gravitational interactions is required to produce variations in transit as observed in blue and red shifts, thus extending the cloud's lifetime to 504 days with particles measuring 0.6 microns in diameter. In both scenarios, we see a clear disparity between theoretical models of particle size and the observed disparity in various telescopes' wavelength capacities. Ultimately, our study is indicative of a planet that is in a state of continuous disintegration and is crucial in facilitating an understanding of the planet's environment and processes that are associated with disintegration. As a result, this system is deemed particularly valuable for future studies in the field of exoplanetary systems. Digital figures 11 and data tables 4 available online. We develop a novel algebro-geometric approach to studying the Milnor fibration and establish a significant condition for holomorphic function deformations to maintain the Milnor fibration intact. In consequence, we derive a strategy to divide the space of polynomials with a specified degree into discrete, localized segments where the diffeomorphism of the Milnor fibration remains unchanged within each category. Additionally, we create a finite set of parameters that fully characterize each localization. Furthermore, we categorize all localization types of quadratic functions and provide a comprehensive inventory of such types, along with descriptive labels. Lastly, we suggest possible avenues for future investigation into higher-degree polynomial functions. In the process, we develop novel applications of discrete algebraic geometry, including the design of specialized tubes to ensure connectivity in certain parameter ranges and the creation of an association between restriction monodromy and the geometric preservation of the Milnor fibration. Equivalently, we investigate the geometric properties of fibration stability across families of holomorphic functions, which holds significant implications for various mathematical theories, as well as their connections to topological invariant properties. Specifically, we observe that restriction monodromy is a topological invariant property, as the fibration's geometric preservation is a necessary condition for its absence in non-localized cases. Conversely, we prove that fibration stability is not solely defined by restriction monodromy, highlighting the complexity of this mathematical concept. Moreover, our study has practical implications for analyzing the properties of hyperplane arrangements, as seen in the classification of Lobel functions, a special case of polynomials where their fibration maintains diffeomorphism structure. I challenge the conventional view of Galileo's influence on science by suggesting that he struggled with mathematical proficiency. This perceived weakness drove him to focus on experimentation and empiricism, as well as embracing the telescope's capabilities. His emphasis on hands-on research, which is often credited as an innovative aspect of his scientific approach, might actually be a consequence of his inability to make meaningful mathematical contributions. Similarly, his extensive discussion of basic scientific principles was, arguably, an outcome of his limitations in mathematics, as they often say "those who can't do, teach." It is proposed that Galileo's scientific vision, which is typically viewed as groundbreaking, was actually based on long-established ideas from mathematicians. The main difference lies in that Galileo chose to articulate these ideas in philosophical writing, as his mathematical colleagues were too preoccupied with advancing scientific work to bother doing the same. Ultimately, it is suggested that we reevaluate our understanding of Galileo's influence on the scientific method to one where his weaknesses, as a mathematician, actually strengthened his strengths, as a scientist. Historians have consistently observed that areas of inquiry where the practitioners are also accomplished mathematicians tend to receive more attention and support. In contrast, sciences reliant more heavily on experimentation and observation, as was the case with Galileo, often benefit from greater philosophical input. This dynamic is not unique to Galileo's time, as we see similar dynamics at play in the relationships between other prominent scientists and mathematicians. In conclusion, Galileo's reputation as a trailblazing scientist is built on a more complex narrative where his weaknesses as a mathematician actually opened the door for his strengths as a scientist and philosopher. It is proposed that we adopt a more nuanced perspective on the interplay between mathematics and science, as demonstrated by Galileo's story, as well as other iconic figures, such as Kepler and Leonardo da Vinci. This revised perspective can serve as a valuable resource for communicating the distinct roles that mathematics and science play in shaping our understanding of the world, as well as their interconnectedness. In addition, it provides an opportunity to reexamine the common assertion that "those who can't do, teach," by suggesting that "those who can do, teach and explain." Moreover, it emphasizes the significance of clear and accessible communication in the pursuit of scientific inquiry. As a testament to Galileo's influence, his legacy continues to inspire scientists, as well as philosophers, regardless of his mathematical abilities.
